findings.rationale: CT's updates are anomalous (median norm ratio ~6.3, mean cos to the median update -0.83, strongly against the federation direction), and its local performance is badly degraded: AUC 0.54 (z=-8.5), ECE 0.22, CITL -0.21 with observed prevalence 0.35 vs mean predicted 0.14. Prevalence is elevated from round 1 with no feature drift, and the O/E ratio is ~2.2-2.7 in every sex subgroup. A low AUC with an inflated outcome rate indicates flipped labels rather than a shift in feature distribution or a poisoned upload alone.

MN (largest of the three, n=2103) shows the same signature: AUC 0.54 (z=-8.6), ECE 0.21, CITL -0.21 with prevalence 0.345 vs mean predicted 0.136. Its updates are anomalous (median norm ratio ~8.9, mean cos -0.85). Subgroup O/E ratios are ~2.5-2.7 across sex groups and ~5-6 in age group 5 and income group 3. Prevalence inflation is present from round 1 with no drift.

VT shows the same pattern: AUC 0.52 (z=-8.9), ECE 0.20, CITL -0.19 with prevalence 0.326 vs mean predicted 0.134. Updates are anomalous (median norm ratio ~5.9, mean cos -0.79). Subgroup O/E ratios are ~2.2-2.8 across sex groups and ~15 in age group 4. Elevated prevalence relative to features is present from round 1 with no drift in features.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with updates, local performance, drift, feature-tail and subgroup views (budget 20 total, fully spent). Three clients (CT, MN, VT) stand out consistently across every screen: anomalous update norms and strongly negative cosine to the median update, local AUC about 0.52-0.54 (far below the federation's 0.78 pooled), CITL about -0.2 with observed prevalence around 0.33-0.35 against predicted ~0.14, and O/E ratios of 2-3 in every sex subgroup. Their feature distributions show no drift from round 1 onward. The AUC collapse together with inflated outcomes points to flipped labels (label_noise) rather than poisoning, since local data is itself corrupted. Other flags (GU mean_cos z=-3.2, GU/DE/NC/WY/TN/ID feature-tail outliers, small-client drift blips in DC/GU/TN/VI/NM/WY) were weak (|z_noise| about 3-5 on small clients, no second independent confirmation) and were not reported. No drift, missing-artefact, explanation-instability, or free-rider signal was found.
